findings.paper_title: 13i Appendix A - Q1 Treasury Management Update
findings.headline: PWLB borrowing rates expected to fall from 5.6–6.1% to 4.3–4.9% over three years
findings.detail: Treasury advisors' forecasts as at 21 September 2026 project gradual reduction in PWLB borrowing rates over the next three years. Bank Rate is forecast to rise from current 3.75% to 4.00% by December, with subsequent direction described as evenly balanced.
findings.matters: Expected fall in PWLB borrowing costs materially improves the financial outlook if the authority needs to take external borrowing.
findings.figures: PWLB rates currently 5.6–6.1%, forecast 4.3–4.9% over three years; Bank Rate 3.75% forecast to 4.00% by December
findings.quote: PWLB interest rates on borrowing are expected to gradually reduce from the current rates of around 5.6% to 6.1%, depending on the term of the loan to between 4.3% and 4.9% over the next 3 years.

findings.paper_title: 13i Appendix A - Q1 Treasury Management Update
findings.headline: Police Fund capital programme reduced £7m to £18m; borrowing need £18m, down £6m from original forecast
findings.detail: Police Fund capital programme has fallen from £25m to £18m since the treasury management strategy was approved in March 2026. With no capital resources available, borrowing requirement is £18m, representing a £6m reduction from the original forecast of £24m.
findings.matters: Reduced capital spend and lower borrowing requirement improve the Police Fund's financial position compared to original forecast.
findings.figures: Capital programme £25m reduced to £18m; borrowing need £18m (down from £24m original forecast)
findings.quote: The value of the Police Fund capital programme has fallen from £25m to £18m since the indicator was set in the TM Strategy. As there are no capital resources to fund this there is a borrowing need of £18m.

findings.paper_title: 13i Appendix A - Q1 Treasury Management Update
findings.headline: MCA capital programme reduced to £255m with no underlying borrowing requirement
findings.detail: Capital programme has been reduced from original estimate of £274m to £255m, with corresponding reduction in capital resources required. MCA requires no external borrowing to fund its programmed capital investment in 2026/27.
findings.matters: Confirms the MCA can fund capital spending from internal resources without incurring new external debt.
findings.figures: Original capital estimate £274m, revised to £255m; capital funding £255m; MCA borrowing need £0m
findings.quote: it remains the case that the MCA has no underlying need to borrow to fund its programmed capital investment in 2026/27.

findings.paper_title: 13i Appendix A - Q1 Treasury Management Update
findings.headline: Police grant payment timing change reduces Police Fund investment income forecast to £1.0m from budget of £3.7m
findings.detail: Police grant is now being paid in monthly instalments instead of upfront in April as in prior years. This results in lower cash balances throughout the year, with funds held in lower-yielding money market funds and call accounts rather than fixed-term deposits.
findings.matters: Material change in grant payment timing affects Police Fund cash flow management and liquidity planning throughout the year.
findings.figures: Police Fund investment income forecast £1.0m vs budget £3.7m
findings.quote: When the budget was set it was assumed that the Police grant would be paid up front in April as was the case in 2025/26. Instead, the Police grant is being paid in monthly instalments which has resulted in reduced cash balances and lower investment income.

findings.paper_title: 13i Appendix A - Q1 Treasury Management Update
findings.headline: MCA treasury investment income forecast £17.6m above annual budget
findings.detail: Treasury income was budgeted at £15.4m but is now forecast at £33.0m. The outperformance reflects higher opening balances from 2025/26 underspends, upfront receipt of integrated settlement funds in April 2026, and interest rates exceeding forecast when the budget was set.
findings.matters: Material upside in treasury income reduces pressure on cash flow and external borrowing requirements.
findings.quote: The budgeted treasury income for the year for the MCA is £15.4m and the current forecast is for income of £33.0m so returns are projected to exceed the budgeted treasury investment income for the year by £17.6m.

findings.headline: Some operational risks showing improvement following targeted management action
findings.detail: Positive movement has been recorded in Strategic Transport Model, Health and Safety Team Capacity, Housing and Strategic Planning Readiness, and Transition Deadline risks, all reduced following delivery of mitigation activity.
findings.matters: Evidence that management action reduces risk scores in specific areas demonstrates organizational capacity to implement mitigation strategies and provides assurance about risk management effectiveness.
findings.figures: Four operational risks reduced in score
findings.quote: Positive movement has been recorded in a number of operational risks. The Strategic Transport Model, Health and Safety Team Capacity, Housing and Strategic Planning Readiness, and Delay in Decisions Affecting Transition Deadline risks have all reduced in score following delivery of mitigation activity

findings.headline: New police fund strategic risk added reflecting emerging funding uncertainty
findings.detail: Two new strategic risks have been added during the reporting period, including a Police Fund risk. This reflects emerging uncertainties in the external environment linked to policing reform and associated funding implications.
findings.matters: A new police-related funding risk likely reflects national changes in policing arrangements creating funding uncertainty for the authority, which could impact its financial position and budget flexibility.
findings.figures: Police Fund added as strategic risk STR0056
findings.quote: two new strategic risks have been added (STR0055 Scale and Pace of Change and STR0056 Police Fund).

findings.headline: Majority of strategic risks continue to sit above the organization's risk appetite
findings.detail: Although the strategic risk profile remains broadly stable, the majority of strategic risks continue to exceed the organization's defined risk appetite. This reflects ongoing acknowledgement that the authority operates above acceptable risk levels.
findings.matters: An organization where most strategic risks sit above appetite indicates governance concern that risk levels are unsustainable, suggesting weakened operational resilience and reduced ability to respond to external shocks.
findings.figures: 10 strategic risks total, with majority above appetite
findings.quote: although the majority of strategic risks continue to sit above risk appetite.

findings.headline: Resource constraints and financial pressures are the most prevalent drivers of risk, with seven of nine identified risk drivers increasing
findings.detail: The analysis of underlying risk drivers shows resource constraints remain the most common driver of risk, followed by financial and budgetary pressures. Seven of the nine principal risk drivers increased during the reporting period, indicating worsening external pressures.
findings.matters: Increasing resource and financial pressures indicate the authority faces sustained structural challenges in delivering services cost-effectively, which affects its capacity to manage commitments and absorb further shocks.
findings.figures: Seven of nine identified risk drivers increasing; resource constraints most prevalent
findings.quote: Resource constraints remain the most prevalent driver of risk, followed by financial and budgetary pressures and uncertainty and change within the external environment.

findings.headline: Insufficient capacity to deliver remains the highest strategic risk with 16 linked operational risks
findings.detail: Insufficient Capacity to Deliver is identified as one of the highest scoring strategic risks. It is linked to 16 Level 2 operational risks, indicating a systemic capacity challenge across the organization. The authority continues to acknowledge delivery demands are exceeding current capacity.
findings.matters: A systemic capacity shortage affecting 16 operational areas suggests the authority is struggling to meet delivery demands across services, which impacts its ability to implement strategy and manage financial commitments.
findings.figures: Insufficient Capacity to Deliver linked to 16 Level 2 risks
findings.quote: Insufficient Capacity to Deliver now has 16 linked Level 2 risks, while Cyber Security Threat and Attack continues to be supported by six associated operational risks.

findings.headline: Police Fund borrowing need reduced to £9m from forecast £49m
findings.detail: The Police Fund's originally forecast borrowing need of £49m for 2026/27 has been reduced to £9m due to higher cash balances and lower capital expenditure forecasts. The MCA itself has no planned borrowing need for 2026/27.
findings.matters: A major reduction in planned borrowing requirement changes debt management strategy, reduces need to access debt markets, and lowers expected borrowing costs.
findings.quote: It was originally forecast that the Police Fund would need to borrow £49m in 2026/27. Due to higher than forecast cash balances at the end of 2025/26 and lower forecast capital expenditure in 2026/27 it is now projected that the Police Fund will have a reduced borrowing need of £9m in 2026/27.

findings.headline: Police Fund investment income forecast at £1.0m against budget of £3.7m due to changed grant payment timing
findings.detail: The budget assumed the Police grant would be paid up front in April as in 2025/26. Instead it is being paid in monthly instalments, which has resulted in lower investment income. The Police Fund held £12.3m of short-term investments as at 30 June 2026.
findings.matters: A material shortfall in investment income signals a change in cash receipt timing that affects liquidity management and the pool of cash available for investment returns.
findings.figures: Forecast £1.0m, budget £3.7m (£2.7m negative variance); Police Fund investments £12.3m as at 30/06/2026
findings.quote: The investment income for the police fund is forecast to be £1.0m compared to a budget of £3.7m. When the budget was set it was assumed that the Police grant would be paid up front in April as was the case in 2025/26.

findings.headline: MCA forecast investment income of £33.0m against budget of £15.4m
findings.detail: Due to the maintenance of significant cash balances and interest rates not falling as predicted, the MCA's investment income forecast is significantly higher than budgeted. The MCA held £827.4m of investments as at 30 June 2026 split between long- and short-term holdings.
findings.matters: Better than budgeted investment income improves the authority's financial position and reduces pressure to find savings elsewhere.
findings.figures: Forecast income £33.0m, budget £15.4m (£17.6m positive variance); total investments £827.4m as at 30/06/2026
findings.quote: Due to the maintenance of significant cash balances and interest rates not falling as predicted by national agencies and advisors, the forecast treasury management income for the MCA is significantly higher than budgeted. Forecast income for the MCA is £33.0m against a budget of £15.4m.

findings.headline: City Region Sustainable Transport Settlement has 18 schemes requiring commitment by March 2027 with 3-4 presenting significant challenges
findings.detail: Residual risk 12 (medium/high) reflects scale and funding constraints of the programme. Of the 18 schemes that must be contractually committed by March 2027, 3-4 are being closely monitored due to significant delivery challenges. Additional CRSTS revenue funding of £9.6m allocated for 2025-26 is supporting the current programme and future development.
findings.matters: Finance directors and lenders track capital programme delivery against fixed deadlines; schemes at risk of missing commitment dates may require rephasing of funding or deprioritization, affecting spend profiles and financial planning.
findings.figures: 18 schemes requiring commitment by March 2027; 3-4 with significant challenges; £9.6m additional CRSTS revenue for 2025-26; residual risk 12
findings.quote: There are currently 18 schemes that need to be contractually committed by March 2027. Of these, 3 to 4 schemes present significant challenges and are being closely monitored through regular meetings with scheme promoters to review progress, address risks, and agree mitigation measures.

findings.headline: Insufficient Capacity to Deliver remains at inherent level of 20 with no mitigation progress and 16 subordinate risks
findings.detail: Strategic risk STR0049 shows no movement from inherent score to residual score (both 20), both rated above appetite. The risk carries 16 child risks with 5 rated medium/high, indicating significant cascade of operational risks. ASRC has previously challenged whether the risk's target score of 4 remains realistic given no improvement over time despite mitigation efforts.
findings.matters: An organization unable to reduce capacity constraints despite targeted mitigation signals governance weakness and potential inability to deliver on strategic commitments or absorb future growth, which affects lender and peer confidence.
findings.figures: 16 child risks identified, 5 with residual medium/high; inherent 20, residual 20, target 4
findings.quote: This risk currently has 16 child risks, 5 of which have a residual score of 'med/high'.
